messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑condition) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------| | In | locative preposition introducing the domain “all parts” | Em | in | OK | | tutte | universal quantifier adjective “all” | todas | all | OK | | parti | set of spatial divisions of the world | partes | parts | OK | | impera | “He governs each part” (exerts rule) | governa | governs | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction linking predicates | e | and | OK | | quivi | adverb locating the second predicate “there” | lá | there | OK | | regge | “He reigns” (holds sovereign authority) | reina | reigns | OK | | quivi *(second occurrence)* | adverb locating existence statements “there” | Lá | there | OK | | è | copular verb asserting existence | está | is/stands | OK | | la | definite article (fem. sing.) marking “città” | sua | (article omitted – possession expressed by “sua”) | UNNECESSARY* | | sua | possessive adjective “His” | sua | his | OK | | città | noun “city” (the Sovereign’s urban domain) | cidade | city | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction | e | and | OK | | l’ | definite article (masc. sing., elided) preceding “alto” | o | the | OK | | alto | adjective “lofty” qualifying the seat | alto | lofty | OK | | seggio | noun “seat” (throne) | trono | throne/seat | OK | | oh | interjection vocative “O” | Ó | O | OK | | felice | adjective describing the emotional state “happy” | feliz | happy | OK | | colui | pronoun referring to the elected individual “he” | aquele | that one / he | OK | | cu' | relative pronoun “whom” introducing the clause | que | who/whom | OK | | ivi | adverb locating the act of election “there” | lá | there | OK | | elegge | verb “elects” (He selects) | escolhe | elects/chooses | OK |

### Summary of Issues - **UNNECESSARY**: the article *la* in “la sua città” does not have a direct counterpart in Portuguese; the translation omits it, which is natural for Portuguese grammar. No other source items are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Portuguese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
